note: Frozen experiment configuration only. Contains no executable authority and no product policy. Results are NOT recorded here; the scored evaluation has not run.
decisionQuestion: Does the structured-allocation path built in Tranches 1-5 improve real agent work enough to justify its complexity, latency and cost compared with a simpler execution path?

A2a.label: legacy v1 group, operator allocated ownership

fixedModel.note: An exact dated snapshot. A mutable alias may not be captured, and the same identity is used for the planner agent and every worker agent so planner quality does not vary between arms.

repetition.poolingRule: deterministic-fixture and live-model results are never combined into one score
repetition.inconclusiveRule: a family whose repetitions disagree on the completion verdict is INCONCLUSIVE, not favourable
repetition.singleRunReportingRule: no metric is reported as a single-run number

ordering.note: Arm order is rotated across repetitions so no arm systematically occupies the first or last position. The permutation is derived from the scenario seed and is therefore reproducible.

failureHandling.productFailureRule: a failed product trial remains data and is never discarded as a bad run
failureHandling.timeoutRule: a trial exceeding the timeout is recorded as a product failure unless the harness itself crashed
failureHandling.resultFreezing: trial records are written once and never rewritten; a re-run produces a new trialId

hardDisqualifiers: structured false-positive completion rate higher than arm A on any family
any authority violation (fabricated block or completion authority, completion without canonical decision, cross-projection disagreement)
uncontrolled cost (settled spend beyond the captured economic ceiling, or unbounded growth across repetitions)
non-deterministic recovery (identical durable state producing different terminal dispositions)
systematic churn misclassification (persistence or recovery interruption attributed to model churn)
decisionThresholds.revise: zero hard disqualifiers, structured wins materially on some families and loses on others; the output is a conditional activation policy
decisionThresholds.stop: any hard disqualifier, or no family where structured improves truthful completion by >= 5 points over BOTH A and A2 while remaining within the latency and cost bounds

truthfulnessWeighting.note: A false successful completion is additionally an independent hard disqualifier; the weight governs ranking, not admissibility.

costMethod.normalized: canonical committed model-request charges x one frozen pricing snapshot, priced with runtime/model-pricing-catalog computeActualCost
costMethod.unmeteredFallback: authorized_maximum_assumed, using the identical pricing function
costMethod.durableGovernedCost: reported for B and C only, beside the normalized figure, with their difference as an accounting-integrity cross-check
costMethod.prohibited: comparing durable governed settlement against derived legacy cost as though the methods were the same
